# runner-synchroniser

Keeps an agent runner's model credentials alive across task replacement.

The Evident runner is a container that can be stopped and replaced at any time — it
scales to zero when idle, and its host task is disposable. Anything that lives only on
its disk is lost with it, including the two things that are expensive to recreate: the
credentials a human bootstrapped interactively (a Claude subscription login, an OpenCode
provider auth) and the agent's session history.

This package is the credential half of that durability story: it restores both
credential stores from an object store at boot, uploads them again whenever they change,
and answers the "does this runner have any way to authenticate a model?" question that
the boot script gates on. It also renders the `litestream.yml` that covers the session
database, so both halves read their bucket, prefix and paths from one config module
instead of two.

It is a CLI, not a library, invoked by two consumers — the Fargate runner image and the
MicroVM image — both of which install the published package and invoke it by name
(`runner-synchroniser <command>`).

## Install

The package is published to npm as `@evident-ai/runner-synchroniser`, exposing one
`runner-synchroniser` binary and requiring Node >= 22.13.0:

```bash
npx @evident-ai/runner-synchroniser@dev env
```

`dist/cli.js` is a single self-contained ESM bundle with **no runtime dependencies** —
the AWS SDK is bundled at build time, so installing it pulls nothing else in.

### Versioning

The package's version **tracks the product release version**, exactly like
`@evident-ai/cli`. `latest` is published on a product release, at the release
version. `dev` is published on every merge to `main` that touches this package or
the root `package.json`, at `<root major>.<minor>.<patch+1>-dev.<sha>`, so `dev`
stays strictly ahead of `latest`.

The version committed in this package's `package.json` is **vestigial** — CI
overwrites it before every publish. This is why `latest` jumped straight from
`0.1.0` to `3.x.y`: the `0.1.x` line predates the policy, not a missing
major-version story, and because npm publishes are immutable that jump is
permanent.

Both consumers install the published package behind the same
`ARG RUNNER_SYNCHRONISER_VERSION=dev`, resolved to a concrete version at image
build time.

## Commands

| Command                        | stdout                                  | Exit codes                                               |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `env`                          | resolved config as shell-eval'able vars | `0` = ran; non-zero = tool broken                        |
| `litestream-config`            | the generated `litestream.yml`          | `0` = ran; non-zero = tool broken                        |
| `restore <claude\|opencode>`   | —                                       | `0` = ran; non-zero = tool broken                        |
| `sync-once <claude\|opencode>` | —                                       | `0` = uploaded (per-runner) or published/adopted/unchanged/absent/disabled (shared vault); `40` = not persisted this tick; other = tool broken |
| `model-auth-ready`             | —                                       | `0` = ready, `10` = not ready; other = tool broken       |
| `self-stop`                    | —                                       | `0` = stopped, `20` = keep the task; other = tool broken |
| `session-db-classify <litestream-restore-exit-code> <attempt> [--on-unusable-replica=<prune\|leave\|clear\|crash>] [--recovery-occurred] [--fresh-db-fallback]` | — | `0` = restored/no-replica/disabled, `32` = re-run and ask again, `31` = unusable (booted fresh, replicates into the existing prefix), `30` = fatal; other = usage/tool broken |
| `session-db-verify <litestream-config-path>` | — | `0` = healthy/skipped/walked-back, `33` = exhausted after verified separation and local disposal, `34` = separation or disposal could not be proven; other = usage/tool broken |

`self-stop` scales this agent's own ECS service to `desiredCount=0` on a clean idle exit
(see Configuration for `CLUSTER`/`SERVICE`/`EVIDENT_SELFSTOP_ROLE_ARN`). It exits `0`
**only** on a confirmed `desiredCount` of 0.

Everything the operator needs to read goes to **stderr**, prefixed `[auth-persistence]`,
so a caller can safely capture stdout. The prefix now covers more than credentials — the
ECS scale-to-zero messages carry it too. It is deliberately **not** renamed to something
broader: `src/logger.ts` marks it verbatim because operator greps and CloudWatch filters
match on that exact string, so widening what it labels is cheaper than breaking every
saved query.

### `session-db-classify`

Implementation-facing reference for the 7th command: it decides what a just-run `litestream restore` of `opencode.db` means and, on attempt 2 only, may run a recovery strategy against S3. `runner/docker-images/fargate/README.md`'s [Strategy/What/Cost table](../docker-images/fargate/README.md#when-the-replica-is-unusable-evident_on_unusable_replica) is the operator-facing view of the same command — this section doesn't restate it.

#### Activity recovery report

Reportable recovery outcomes append one versioned JSON line to the session-DB recovery
report. `evident run` drains that file once after authentication and records the outcome in
the runner activity log. Healthy boots do not write a report. An initial restore failure writes
a warning `restore_retried` record before the retry's result is known. Writing is best-effort
and never changes this command's exit code. The CLI reader owns this record contract: add a new
`v` rather than repurposing a field.

MicroVM boot-shell give-ups use that same JSONL contract and path. The hook truncates the
report at the start of each `/run`, so a later startup decision supersedes an earlier one;
`/resume` preserves the current report. Their `replication_suspended` field is `true`, meaning
that start is not backing up its new session history. The normal mapper defaults the field to
`false`; the MicroVM `--fresh-db-fallback` outcome is also `true` because it cannot safely
replicate that boot.

#### Positionals

| Positional                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<litestream-restore-exit-code>` | Status of the `litestream restore` the shell just ran. `0` → stat the local DB; any non-zero → the recovery ladder below. The value itself is never inspected (a Go panic `2` is treated exactly like a `1`). |
| `<attempt>`                      | 1-based (`/^\d+$/`, `>= 1`) — the sole mutation gate.                                                                                    |

#### The attempt ladder

| Attempt | Behaviour                                                     |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1       | Plain retry — **zero S3 calls, not even the probe**.              |
| 2       | The **only** attempt that may probe or mutate S3.                 |
| ≥ 3     | Gives up **before** the probe.                                    |

`entrypoint.sh` caps its retry loop at a hard-coded `3` as a real second bound: the classifier is stateless per invocation, so nothing except that loop stops attempt 2 from being asked twice.

#### `--on-unusable-replica` flag syntax

- Only the `=`-joined form (`--on-unusable-replica=leave`); the space-separated form is rejected.
- Position-free.
- Repeating the flag is rejected, even with the same value both times.
- Any other `--` token is rejected.
- Every rejection exits `2` (`EXIT_USAGE`) with the usage message — **never** a silent fall-back to the destructive default.

#### Recovery-report flags

`--recovery-occurred` marks a later successful restore after this boot already recovered a
replica, so an empty result is reported as a fresh session database. `--fresh-db-fallback`
marks a runtime that intentionally has no retry budget and will therefore boot fresh after this
otherwise-transient failure. Each flag may appear once, does not change the command's exit code,
and is rejected when repeated.

On the MicroVM's one-attempt path, `--fresh-db-fallback` also means the fresh database does not
replicate during that boot.

#### Outcome → exit code

| Outcome                                        | Code | When                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `disabled`                                      | `0`  | bucket or prefix unset — short-circuits **before** the exit code is examined     |
| `restored`                                      | `0`  | restore exit `0` and the local DB is non-empty                                   |
| `noReplica`                                     | `0`  | restore exit `0` but the DB is absent or zero-byte                               |
| `retryTransient`                                | `32` | restore failed, attempt 1 — no probe, no S3 call at all                          |
| `recovered`                                     | `32` | attempt 2, a successful `prune` (1 key) or any `clear` (including a partial one)  |
| `unusableReplica(strategy)`                     | `31` | attempt 2, `leave`                                                                |
| `unusableReplica(attemptsExhausted)`            | `31` | attempt ≥ 3, before the probe                                                     |
| `unusableReplica(targetHealthy)`                | `31` | attempt 2, `prune`; the newest L0 isn't provably corrupt AND the escalation declined (unreadable, or nothing parses) |
| `unusableReplica(noL0Present)`                  | `31` | attempt 2, `prune`; the prefix is **empty**, so there is nothing to prune and nothing to quarantine |
| `unusableReplica(layoutMismatch)`               | `31` | attempt 2, `prune`; objects exist under the prefix but **none** parse as an LTX key at all — **a bug**, see below |
| `unusableReplica(recoveryFailed)`               | `31` | attempt 2, `prune`'s delete itself threw, or the quarantine escalation moved nothing |
| `recovered(quarantine)`                         | `32` | attempt 2, `prune` found nothing at L0 but the damage is deeper: the replica was moved aside |
| `fatal(misconfig)`                              | `30` | no object store while persistence is enabled, or the probe failed on attempt 2   |
| `fatal(deliberate)`                             | `30` | attempt 2, `crash`                                                                |

Fatal exit codes 30 and 34 are reported directly to `POST /v1/runners/self/startup-failure`
before the CLI starts. Reporting is best-effort and never changes the exit code.

`31` also guarantees local debris (`opencode.db`, `-wal`, `-shm`) is discarded, one `try` per path, at the classifier's single return point. Note `32` isn't purely "transient" — `recovered` shares it with `retryTransient` even though a `recovered` outcome already mutated S3.

The probe is a `list`, not a `get`: S3 answers a wrong bucket name with `NoSuchBucket`, also a 404, so a `get`-based probe would read a misconfigured bucket as healthy and unlock recovery against it.

#### Boot size signals

Two markers report the numbers a boot already computes but used to throw away (#1113):

| Marker | Emitted from | When it fires | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SESSION-DB-SIZE` | `describeSessionDbClassification` (`diagnostics.ts`) | Once per `session-db-classify` invocation that reaches `restored` or `noReplica` — i.e. every boot where the restore exit code was `0`. `disabled` and every non-zero-exit outcome (`retryTransient`, `recovered`, `unusableReplica`, `fatal`) never `stat` the local DB, so they emit no size. | `state` (`restored`\|`empty`\|`absent`), `bytes` |
| `SESSION-DB-REPLICA-SIZE` | `probeReplica` (`replica-recovery.ts`), its `ok` branch | Only on attempt 2's probe, i.e. only after a **failed** first restore — see the caveat below. | `objects`, `bytes` |

**Format convention:** `<MARKER>: <prose> <k>=<v> … bytes=<n>`, with the machine-readable
fields appended at the end of the line and `bytes` always last:

```
SESSION-DB-SIZE: <prose> state=<restored|empty|absent> bytes=<n>
SESSION-DB-REPLICA-SIZE: <prose> objects=<m> bytes=<n>
```

Numbers go last because a CloudWatch Logs Insights `parse` capture needs a **literal
delimiter after every capture except the final one**, which runs to end of line — free
prose after a capture would make the pattern ambiguous. `diagnostics.test.ts` and
`replica-recovery.test.ts` each pin a line matching `/ (state=\w+ )?bytes=\d+$/`, so an
edit that appends prose after the number breaks a test rather than silently breaking an
operator's saved query.

**Logs Insights queries** (copy-pasteable, and the reason the format above is fixed):

Session-DB size distribution across the fleet:

```
fields @timestamp, @message
| parse @message "SESSION-DB-SIZE: * state=* bytes=*" as dbProse, dbState, dbBytes
| filter ispresent(dbBytes)
| stats count(*) as boots,
        avg(dbBytes) as avgBytes,
        pct(dbBytes, 50) as p50Bytes,
        pct(dbBytes, 95) as p95Bytes,
        max(dbBytes) as maxBytes
  by bin(1d)
| sort @timestamp desc
```

Growth curve, and how many boots restored nothing:

```
fields @timestamp, @message
| parse @message "SESSION-DB-SIZE: * state=* bytes=*" as dbProse, dbState, dbBytes
| filter ispresent(dbState)
| stats count(*) as boots, max(dbBytes) as maxBytes by dbState, bin(1d)
```

Replica size + object count (ECS, failed-first-restore boots only — see the caveat below):

```
fields @timestamp, @message
| parse @message "SESSION-DB-REPLICA-SIZE: * objects=* bytes=*" as replicaProse, replicaObjects, replicaBytes
| filter ispresent(replicaBytes)
| stats max(replicaBytes) as maxReplicaBytes, max(replicaObjects) as maxObjects by bin(1d)
```

**Caveat: the two markers have very different fleet coverage.** `SESSION-DB-SIZE` fires
on **every healthy boot on both runtimes** and is the fleet-wide growth-curve signal.
`SESSION-DB-REPLICA-SIZE` fires **only** on ECS's attempt 2 — i.e. only when a first
restore already failed — and essentially never on the MicroVM, whose hook hard-codes the
classify attempt to `1` (`common.sh:352`), which never reaches the probe. Chart
`SESSION-DB-SIZE` for growth; treat `SESSION-DB-REPLICA-SIZE` as a diagnostic for
failed-restore boots only, or an empty series will look like a broken signal instead of
what it is.

#### The four `--on-unusable-replica` strategies

- **`prune` (default)** — ≤1 guarded delete iff the newest L0's own bytes fail the LTX header check (`length >= 100` and magic `"LTX1"`) → `recovered`/`32`; a failed delete (`recoveryFailed`) or a declined escalation → `31`. **Header-only** check: a valid header with deeper corruption is judged sound and left alone by the *delete* — and since #1106 that is no longer the end of the road. When prune finds nothing to delete (`targetHealthy`/`noL0Present`) **and** at least one key parses as an LTX object, it **escalates to quarantine**: every object under `<prefix>/opencode.db/` is moved to `<prefix>/quarantine/opencode.db/<timestamp>/` → `recovered(quarantine)`/`32`. It does **not** escalate on `layoutMismatch` (we don't understand the layout), on an unreadable object (absent evidence), or on an empty prefix. Never prunes twice.
- **`leave`** — zero S3 mutation → `31`. Cost is "prior history lost this boot". The fresh local DB replicates into the existing prefix; no new chain is started. Upside: the runner still comes online without a crash loop.
- **`clear`** — deletes every key under `<prefix>/opencode.db/` passing `isDeletableReplicaKey`; that guard, not the `list()` prefix, is the boundary (IAM grants `s3:DeleteObject*` bucket-wide). One `try` per key. A **parti
…[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]…
cannot self-stop" and exits `20` (keep the task). Ignored by every other command. |
| `EVIDENT_SELFSTOP_ROLE_ARN` †             | Role `self-stop` assumes for its ECS calls.                              | Optional: falls back to the task role's own credentials. A failed/incomplete assume-role → `20`. |

`runner/docker-images/fargate/README.md` documents these same three from the deployment side —
keep them in sync.

Requiring **both** `LITESTREAM_BUCKET` and `LITESTREAM_PREFIX` (never just one) means
half a location can never produce a malformed key.

The paths and keys that follow from the bucket/prefix:

| Store       | Local path                                | Object key                          |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Claude      | `$HOME/.claude/.credentials.json`         | `<prefix>/claude/credentials.json`  |
| OpenCode    | `$HOME/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`   | `<prefix>/opencode/auth.json`       |
| OpenCode DB | `$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` | `<prefix>/opencode.db` (litestream) |

When persistence is enabled and `CREDENTIAL_VAULT_PREFIX` is set, both credential keys
use that shared prefix instead of `<prefix>`. The OpenCode database continues replicating
under `LITESTREAM_PREFIX`; the vault prefix only redirects the two credential objects. The
Evident CLI resolves this value from the runner's vault binding.

The session database is replicated by litestream itself; this package only generates its
config. `env` emits `PERSISTENCE_BUCKET`, `CLAUDE_CREDS`, `OPENCODE_DB_PATH` and
`CREDS_SYNC_INTERVAL`, each single-quoted so a value containing shell metacharacters is
inert when `eval`'d.

`entrypoint.sh` asserts, right after it `eval`s this output, that each key is *defined*
(not merely non-empty) and splits the four into two groups: a key is **required** — the
shell dies naming it — if it has no safe degradation; it is **tolerated** — the shell logs
a WARNING naming it and carries on — if it does. `OPENCODE_DB_PATH` and
`CREDS_SYNC_INTERVAL` are required: both are dereferenced for real work (deleting/creating
the session DB, sizing the sync-loop sleep), so a guessed value would be actively wrong,
not merely absent. `PERSISTENCE_BUCKET` and `CLAUDE_CREDS` are tolerated: an empty
`PERSISTENCE_BUCKET` is already the designed "persistence disabled" state, and
`CLAUDE_CREDS` is dereferenced only in operator-facing message text. If you change
`renderEnv` to make a required key conditional, the entrypoint will brick every container
running that version — the runner installs this package from a floating npm tag (`dev` /
`latest`), so the shell and the CLI can genuinely be different versions (#779, #821).

## Behaviour worth knowing

- **A non-empty local file that is not valid JSON is protected**, never overwritten and
  never uploaded: it may be unreadable to us and still be the operator's only copy. An
  _empty_ one holds nothing to protect, so it does not block a restore.
- **Valid JSON, not mere existence, is the readiness test** — for both stores, and it is
  re-read on every call, because OpenCode provider auth can be bootstrapped long after
  boot.
- **Restores are atomic**: the object is written to an exclusively-created temporary
  file, `chmod`ed before the secret lands in it, validated, then renamed into place. The
  temporary file is removed on every failure path. Directories end up `700`, credential
  files `600`.
- **Nothing throws out of `restore`/`sync`.** `sync-once` runs on an unsupervised timer,
  where an unguarded failure would silently stop persisting credentials for the rest of
  the task's life. Failures degrade to a warning and are retried on the next tick.
- **Per-runner `sync-once` uploads only on change.** Its last uploaded hash (a sha256, not
  the credentials) is kept in a state file next to the credential file, so every invocation
  is a self-contained process.
- **Shared-vault mode is two-way and conditional.** `sync-once` adopts a changed shared
  credential or publishes a locally changed one with a conditional write. A writer that
  loses the race adopts the winner instead of overwriting it. A `40` exit is an expected
  "not persisted this tick" result, not a broken tool; the polling loop accepts it and
  retries on the next tick.
- **Not-found is distinguished from failed.** A missing object is reported as "nothing to
  restore"; an access or network error is reported as a failure, because that tells the
  operator their persisted credentials may still be recoverable.

### Shared-vault log markers

In shared-vault mode, these markers identify the synchronization result without logging
credential bytes. Hash values are short prefixes and ETags remain opaque:

| Marker | Meaning |
| ------ | ------- |
| `VAULT-MODE` | Both credential stores use the shared vault prefix. |
| `VAULT-PUBLISHED` | A credential was created in, or conditionally replaced in, the vault. |
| `VAULT-ADOPTED` | A valid vault credential was installed locally. |
| `VAULT-CONTENDED` | Another writer won the conditional write, so this runner is adopting its result. |
| `VAULT-CONTENDED-UNRESOLVED` | The winning object could not be read; the next tick will retry. |
| `VAULT-REMOTE-INVALID` | The vault object was not valid JSON and was either replaced or left untouched. |
| `VAULT-REMOTE-UNREADABLE` | The vault read failed; the next tick will retry. |
| `VAULT-NO-ETAG` | Publication was skipped because a remote object had no ETag. |
| `VAULT-ADOPT-FAILED` | A valid vault credential could not be installed locally; the next tick will retry. |

## The `ObjectStore` port

The `ObjectStore` port has seven methods. `get(key)` returns `{ body, etag }` or `null`
when the object is absent; `etag` is an opaque compare-and-swap token and may be `null`
when the store did not report one. `put(key, body)` is the unconditional write used by
per-runner synchronization. `putIfAbsent(key, body)` creates with a conditional
`If-None-Match: *` write, and `putIfMatch(key, body, etag)` replaces with a conditional
`If-Match: <etag>` write. Both return `'written'` or `'conflict'`; only contention
returns `'conflict'`, while every other error throws. `list(prefix)` returns `{ key, size }` entries
(`ObjectSummary[]`) — every object under `prefix`, size in bytes. It throws on any error
and never maps one to `[]` (an empty array means "reached the store, nothing there"); the
adapter owns pagination, and `delete` is idempotent. S3 vocabulary (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`,
the typed `NoSuchKey`/`NotFound` errors) is confined to the single adapter in
`src/s3-object-store.ts`, so the storage backend can be swapped without touching the
restore/sync/classify logic.

The S3 adapter is the only one that exists. It uses no static credentials — auth is
whatever the ambient AWS credential chain resolves (on the Evident runner, the ECS task
role).

## Development

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build      # tsup -> dist/cli.js, a single self-contained ESM bundle
pnpm test       # vitest
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
```

From the repository root, prefix with `pnpm --filter @evident-ai/runner-synchroniser`.

The bundle must stay a **single file**: both consumers need a self-contained
`dist/cli.js` with no sibling chunks — both the Fargate runner image and the
MicroVM image install this package from npm as a `bin`, where `files: ["dist"]`
ships whatever `dist` contains, with no `node_modules` alongside it.
`tsup.config.ts` disables splitting and bundles the AWS SDK so neither consumer
needs anything else.

The restore/sync/CLI tests need neither AWS nor a real filesystem — rather than shimming
a fake `aws` binary onto `PATH`, they inject two ports: `InMemoryObjectStore` (in
`src/object-store.ts`) and `FakeFileOps` (in `src/test-support.ts`). The `FileOps` port
exists specifically for failure injection: the suite runs as root, where a real
`chmod 000` is a no-op, so "a `chmod` that fails must warn and not abort" and "a hash
failure must skip one tick, not kill the loop" are otherwise not reproducible. The real
`nodeFileOps` implementation is tested against a temporary directory.
